basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Quae peperit. Hi qui de Cetura nati sunt occupaverunt terram Trogoditen et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text:
Vers. 2. Quae peperit. Hi qui de Cetura nati sunt occupaverunt terram Trogoditen et Arabiam, quae Eudemon dicitur, usque ad mare Rubrum.

Allegorice sicut per Agar et Ismaelem designantur Judaei in servitutem generati, ita per Ceturam et ejus filios designantur haeretici qui in Novo Testamento | sub praetextu nominis Christi male de ejus veritate fidei senserunt. Unde bene postea Abraham filiis concubinarum munera largitus fuisse dicitur, haereditatem vero solus Isaac consecutus est, quia haereticis Christus in praesenti beneficia scientiae et intelligentiae tribuit, sola autem Ecclesia catholica ad regnum perducitur.
